clue.text: Initially, it appears unusually far-fetched and otherworldly

definitions.text: Initially, it appears unusually far-fetched and otherworldly

blocks.note: surface reading: some first impression strikes one as implausible
setter's reading: a craft said to come from far away, from another world, and whose sightings are rare and doubted

explanation.surface: Someone's first reaction to a story is that it sounds bizarre and unearthly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a reported UFO: sightings are unusual, the visitor has been fetched from afar, and it is not of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc-shaped alien spacecraft is the classic object of doubtful sightings from another planet.

clue.text: Start to moderate a kind of free-for-all

blocks.note: to open is to start
to season is to temper or moderate, as in justice seasoned with mercy

explanation.surface: A chairperson begins to moderate a debate that is becoming a free-for-all.
explanation.definitionFit: An open season is a period when anyone may attack or hunt a target freely, so it is a sort of unrestricted melee.

clue.text: Vital material flowing here - force it on US audience?

blocks.note: surface reading: something essential, like blood or money, in circulation
setter's reading: a liquid from the household supply, and Americans would ask for it from a faucet rather than by the British name

explanation.surface: Some essential substance circulates while someone tries to impose it on American viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The British name uses the word Americans replace with faucet, so you would have to force the term on a US audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking water supplied through household pipes is the life-giving liquid that comes out when you turn the handle.

clue.text: Threads brought together, writing material up found in old jacket

indicators.note: in a down light 'up' means reading upward, so the word for writing material runs backwards
something found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
ink is what pens write with

explanation.surface: A tailor joins threads and works writing material into a historic garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed writing material goes between the last two letters of the old jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Double knit is a fabric made by knitting two sets of yarn together on twin needles, so its threads are joined.

clue.text: Finish drinking with actors, a bit depressed

blocks.note: to down a drink is to finish it in one go
the cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: After the last round with the company of players, someone feels a little low.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means dejected or low in spirits, a mild form of feeling depressed.

clue.text: Stupid dunce, holding creative skill up, not yet found out?

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a muddled one, so these letters are jumbled
in a down light 'up' means reading from bottom to top, so the word for creative skill runs backwards
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
art is creative skill

explanation.surface: A slow pupil with an artistic gift has gone undiscovered so far.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'dunce' hides that the anagrammed word must split in two to wrap round the reversed skill; 'found out' suggests exposed, but here it means located.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untraced has not been tracked down or located, so it remains undiscovered for now.

clue.text: Put out about German finance (and English) favouring the affluent

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the rest

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
the Deutschmark was the German currency before the euro
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about German and English money matters that suit the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed, but the second word is the anagram signal for the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods and services are aimed at richer, more discerning customers.

clue.text: See 4 across
I'm employed to keep planes, etc in good condition

definitions.text: I'm employed to keep planes, etc in good condition

blocks.note: surface reading: an aircraft mechanic who keeps aeroplanes airworthy
setter's reading: the plane is a broad-leaved street species, and with its woody relatives it needs a specialist to prune and treat it

explanation.surface: A worker describes the job of maintaining aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree common in London streets, not an aircraft; the 'etc' hints at oaks and elms too.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who prunes, braces and treats diseased trees keeps the London plane and its relatives healthy.

clue.text: Rather lame as contents of Telegraph on an issue, ie not OTT

blocks.clueFragment: Rather lame as contents of Telegraph on an issue
blocks.note: surface reading: a feeble opinion piece in a newspaper on some topic

blocks.clueFragment: contents of Telegraph on an issue
blocks.note: setter's reading: what lies inside a considered argument, as opposed to excess

explanation.surface: A newspaper's weak column on a topic is dismissed as tame, at least not over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is over the top; the lukewarm piece stays inside the bounds of sense, the phrase taken literally as contained in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept within sensible limits avoids excess, the opposite of going over the top.

clue.text: Present left during function over which there's an icy reception?

definitions.text: over which there's an icy reception?

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the first two pieces sit inside the function

blocks.note: now is the present time
L is the abbreviation for left
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A gift is left during a party where the welcome turns frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party but is the mathematical sine.
explanation.definitionFit: Above the altitude marked by this boundary on a mountain, the ground stays permanently covered in ice and snow.

clue.text: List of accusations citing some bed-linen on the ward?

blocks.note: a ward is someone in your charge
a sheet is a piece of bed-linen

explanation.surface: A hospital ward's linen inventory is mistaken for a police document.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the linen follows the ward. 'Ward' suggests a hospital, but here it means a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge sheet is the police record listing the offences a suspect is formally accused of.

clue.text: Building up a tall story for listeners, usually

definitions.text: Building up a tall story for listeners, usually

blocks.note: surface reading: embroidering an unlikely tale
setter's reading: said out loud, a tall storey, and such a building usually has many tall storeys

explanation.surface: Someone is spinning an exaggerated yarn for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Story and storey sound the same, so the 'tall story' is a high level of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building of many floors reaching upward is what towers over a city.

clue.text: "Green" kids' treats - they're the tops!

blocks.note: vert is green in heraldry and in French
ices are ice creams and lollies children love

explanation.surface: Children's lime ice lollies are hailed as the best.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic term for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertices are the highest points or apexes of shapes, so they are literally the peaks.

clue.text: An extreme case, where people don't normally see the light

definitions.text: An extreme case, where people don't normally see the light

blocks.note: surface reading: an obstinate person who refuses to be converted

blocks.clueFragment: where people don't normally see the light
blocks.note: setter's reading: radiation just beyond the end of the visible spectrum, invisible to human eyes

explanation.surface: A hardliner is so extreme that they never come round to reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the light' means to be converted, but here it is literal: the eye cannot detect this radiation, which sits past the extreme end of the rainbow.
explanation.definitionFit: This band of electromagnetic radiation has wavelengths longer than visible red, so human vision cannot detect it.

clue.text: After 1, squad provided full unofficial version

blocks.note: surface reading: some team mentioned after the first clue; but 1 is the answer to 1 down, whose first word makes the Flying Squad
setter's reading: the slang name for that police unit, given in full rather than shortened

explanation.surface: A team arrives after the first, offering a complete unauthorised edition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a London police unit; in Cockney rhyming slang it is known by this pair of words, usually shortened to 'the Sweeney'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang replaces squad with the name of the fictional demon barber, so the full slang form is this name.

clue.text: Short time with nobody about - given a bit of a rocket?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for nobody goes round the brief time

blocks.note: nobody is no one
sec is short for second

explanation.surface: With nobody around for a moment, someone gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a rocket' is British slang for being reprimanded, but here the rocket is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cone-shaped forward section of a missile or spacecraft is one part of the vehicle.

clue.text: See 8
Back blackleg with some hesitation - not the best for the job

definitions.text: not the best for the job

blocks.note: to back a motion is to second it
a blackleg is a strikebreaker, also called a rat
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A union official hesitantly supports a strikebreaker, who is hardly ideal for the post.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British for a worker who carries on during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-rater is a mediocre person, inferior to the top candidates for a position.

clue.text: See 9
See 15
Personally keeping balanced view of unusually deep fossil

indicators.note: something done unusually is not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A palaeontologist privately holds a level-headed opinion about an oddly buried fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed answer is SELF-POISED, run on into 25 across ('See 21'), but the source data does not link the two lights; this light takes the first four letters of the anagram and 25 across the other six.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poised by one's own effort means maintaining balance and composure without outside support.

clue.text: Extra cover available as insurance against cold weather?

blocks.note: over means extra, as in left over
a coat is a covering, as of paint

explanation.surface: A policy with extra cover protects against winter storms.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is also a cricket fielding position, and cover sounds like insurance, but the words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy outer garment worn over other clothes protects the wearer from chilly conditions.

clue.text: See 1
Back in form to play a game of football?

definitions.text: Back in form to play a game of football?

blocks.note: surface reading: a player recovering their best form for a match
setter's reading: a back is a player positioned at the rear of the team, protecting the goal

explanation.surface: A footballer has regained fitness and is ready to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in form' reads as recovered, but 'Back' is the position: the player who guards the goal area.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-backs and centre-backs are the team members whose job is guarding their own goal against attackers.

clue.text: See 21

definitions.note: the definition is in the clue to 21 down: 'Personally keeping balanced'

blocks.note: the last six letters of the anagram of 'deep fossil' in the clue to 21 down

explanation.walkthrough: This light continues 21 down: the full answer is SELF-POISED, an anagram of 'deep fossil' signalled by 'unusually', though the source data does not link the two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Poised means balanced and composed, the second half of a compound meaning steady through one's own effort.
